review_notes: The Gadpar failure is described as a dry landslide of earth and rock that buried the victim and damaged the house; the source does not establish a distinct rockfall mechanism.
The later Timure account explicitly states that the death toll from the same landslide reached nine.
The article confirms a landslide at Dugunagadhi but does not attribute any death count to that landslide; earthquake casualty figures elsewhere in the story are separate.
The Siddhababa road failure involved mud, soil and rocks falling from the slope; the source reports a landslide and does not establish channelized debris-flow behavior.
The Nyakfedi source describes a mud-and-earth landslide that buried one trekker, who died; it does not provide evidence for a distinct debris-flow classification.
The fresh slide near the third bridge blocked the Narayangadh-Muglin road in both directions and overturned a truck, so the event is a road obstruction.
The Kali Khola slide buried a police vehicle; three officers' bodies were recovered while one officer remained missing, supporting three confirmed deaths.
The Mauwakhola incident is reported as a rain-triggered landslip/mudslide blocking the highway; the evidence does not establish a channelized debris flow.
The Ghansikuwa landslide blocked both directions of the Prithvi Highway and the report focuses on clearing and traffic diversion, making this a road-obstruction event.
The Falleghar slope failure completely blocked the Saljhandi-Dhorpatan road and stranded travelers, so the appropriate event type is road obstruction.
The Timure workers' camp landslide killed two people; the source separately identifies nine people as injured.
The debris-laden flood/landslide struck the ambulance and the elderly patient died; the driver was injured, supporting one confirmed death.
The Galaudi landslide buried two vehicles and obstructed the Prithvi Highway, so this record is best classified as a road-obstruction event.
The later update for the same Timure collapse states that the death toll had risen to eight, superseding the earlier five-death report.
The Torakhet report explicitly states that there were no human or livestock casualties, supporting a confirmed death count of zero.
Six bodies were recovered immediately after the Mallesi landslide and the final missing person was later found dead, bringing confirmed deaths to seven.
Later recovery confirmed all four members of the Gurung household died in the Champadevi-8/Bilandu landslide.
The slide at the third bridge blocked both directions of the Narayangadh-Muglin road and overturned a truck; it is a road-obstruction incident.
The dry slide/rock fall at Dhig Danda buried about 30 metres of the Khandbari-Kimathanka road and stopped traffic, so the event type is road obstruction.
The Kali Khola source describes a mud-laden landslide onto the road; it does not establish the channelized flow behavior needed for a debris-flow classification.
The Dalal road failure is described as a mud-laden landslide from the slope; the article does not demonstrate a channelized debris flow.
The Panchkilo landslide buried part of the Narayangadh-Muglin road and disrupted vehicle movement, supporting road obstruction as the event type.
The Haade Thomko slope failure buried the Gaighat-Diktel road and halted traffic from around 4 a.m., so it is a road-obstruction event.
Sources alternately call the Phyakre River failure a landslide, dry landslide and mudslide; they do not establish a channelized debris-flow mechanism.
